thread:
incident-bot: Alert P3: elevated 5xx on /v1/generate (hosted) — 5m avg 4.2% (threshold 1.0%). paging eng-oncall.
alex_cheng: i'm oncall, pulling metrics now. seeing correlated increase in queue_depth and avg_seq_len. spike started ~03:18 UTC.
priya_narayanan: jumping in. no deploys in last 8h. Interesting: most errors correlate with streaming sessions that keep connections open for long token windows. KV memory pressure also high on pool-redwood-hosted-us-west-2.
mike_jensen: any specific tenants or routes spiking?
sara_ops: telemetry: top error sources are text-generation and chat-stream; tenant heatmap shows top contributors ten420 and ten771. both have long history of long-context runs.
alex_cheng: root-cause working hypothesis: head-of-line blocking from continuous batching where very long sequences (>>1024 tokens) build up KV cache and delay flushes; proxy timeouts kick in. batching config tuned for low latency is producing too-small batches but long queues.
priya_narayanan: mitigation options (live):
- A) increase batching window and batch size to push throughput (will increase median inter-token latency)
- B) decrease window to flush earlier and reduce tail latency but may raise backend pressure and 503s
- C) enable per-tenant long-seq throttles or temporary QPS caps
- D) temporarily disable server-side streaming on suspect pools so long sessions are served with non-streaming fallback (reduces long-lived connections)
We should combine A+C+D for quickest effect.
sam_oncall: agree on combining. prioritize reducing 5xx even if latencies rise. what's safe to flip?
alex_cheng: propose immediate canary in us-west-2 (10% nodes) with these changes:
```
# pool canary changes
rictl pool update pool-redwood-hosted-us-west-2-canary \
  --continuous_batch_min_flush_ms=30 \
  --max_batch_size=300 \
  --enable_kv_eviction=true
# disable streaming at proxy layer for canary
rproxy update-config --pool pool-redwood-hosted-us-west-2-canary --disable-streaming=true
# apply tenant qps cap for heavy tenants
rictl tenant update --tenant-id=ten420 --qps-multiplier=0.75
rictl tenant update --tenant-id=ten771 --qps-multiplier=0.75
```
priya_narayanan: adding a short-lived proxy timeout tweak: increase backend read timeout by 2s to avoid premature 504s while canary warms. ops-bot can we roll canary?
ops-bot: Canary rollout job created job-id=deploy-11988 targeting 10% nodes.
mike_jensen: monitoring: focus on 5xx %, p50/p95 inter-token latency, connection counts, and proxy 504/502 rates. If 5xx < 1% in canary after 8 minutes, expand to 40%.
sara_ops: canary metrics 3m in: 5xx down from 4.2% -> 1.5% in canary slice, p95 latency +220ms, connection count reduced by 18%. backend GPU util down from 96% -> 86% on canary nodes.
sam_oncall: decent signal. expand to 40% now.
ops-bot: Canary job updated: rolling to 40% nodes. job-id=deploy-11988.
alex_cheng: while rolling, also spin up a temporary dedicated long-seq drain pool and migrate queued long requests there. Command: 
```
rictl pool create pool-longseq-temp --gpu-type=a100 --size=4 --annotations="longseq-only"
rictl router add-rule --route long_seq_detected=true --pool pool-longseq-temp
```
priya_narayanan: note: creating pool adds ~2-3m; but will help for sustained runs.
mike_jensen: after 15m of wider roll: global 5xx at 0.8%, p95 +240ms overall. Most enterprise tenants within throttles report degraded throughput but successful completions.
sara_ops: customers reporting slower streaming fill rate; a few internal devs flag chat UX oddities. Adding note to status: "lower error rate; increased latency for long generations; streaming reduced on select pools."
alex_cheng: agree. prepare an incident status update. also set an automated alert to rollback if p50 latency delta > 300ms sustained 10m.
priya_narayanan: follow-up actions to create as tickets: prioritized batching (avoid H-O-L), per-tenant dynamic throttling, smarter KV eviction policy, and streaming-quality fallback to chunked responses.
sam_oncall: handoff in 50m. i'll compile immediate mitigation timeline, commands run, and list of tenants throttled.
ops-bot: Incident action: throttles applied to ten420 and ten771; pool configs updated in canary and expanded.
incident-bot: incident upgraded: now classified as P3 mitigated. incident id=incident-2026-07-02-11988 reference root_ts=1773004321
mike_jensen: next steps: keep current batching for 4 hours, provision more dedicated capacity for long sequences overnight, and evaluate lowering continuous_batch_min_flush_ms in controlled experiments later.
sara_ops: status page updated: "Partial degradation: errors reduced; higher latencies for long-generation requests and limited streaming in some regions. Engineers are monitoring."
alex_cheng: post-mortem notes I'll add: timeline, config diffs, tenant impacts, customer comms, and decision rationale. rolling changes will be reverted to defaults at 02:00 UTC tomorrow unless further regressions observed.
priya_narayanan: creating automated alert: name=Batching_5xx_guard, condition=5xx_rate>1.5% for 5m, notify #eng-oncall and #sre.
ops-bot: Alert rule created: id=alert-9873.
sam_oncall: attaching perf graphs and command logs to incident doc. handing off to priya for follow-ups.
alex_cheng: Thanks all. marking active mitigation resolved; monitoring continues. If errors spike again page eng-oncall. :thumbsup:
priya_narayanan: ack. I'll take over the watch and own the roll-forward tickets.
incident-bot: Incident P3 moved to resolved-mitigated state; log created incident-2026-07-02-11988.
sam_oncall: closing thread after PRs/tickets linked to incident. :white_check_mark:
